bc_keystone_crag.blurb: Keystone Crag is a short, steep sport crag on Quadra Island, in the Chinese Mountains. It sits on the hillside above the Beech's Mountain trail, and a climbers' path also runs across the slope to it from Manzanita Wall. Seven bolted routes range from easy fifth-class up to low 5.11, with most falling around 5.9 and 5.10. Lines run roughly 8 to 22 m, and the wall is built in two tiers split by a ledge. Expect steep ground with friendly holds, plus a few boulder problems in the caves. Climbers praise the quality but note the wall is on the short side.

bc_lower_bear.blurb: Lower Bear is the lowest part of the Bear Country sport area in the KLO Creek drainage, in the Okanagan near Kelowna. Seven bolted routes make up the crag, spanning about 5.9 to 5.12, with two each at 5.9, the 5.10 grades and the 5.11 grades and one at 5.12. The walk in is around 20 minutes along the main trail, over several bridges and a creek crossing on rocks, then a spur trail that crosses back over the water to the middle of the cliff. Water levels can make the crossing risky in spring.
